correctness.rationale: All integer arguments and all nonnegative indices: digit one excluded using polynomial Lucas; for remaining even n, z=0 and z=-1 classes automatically yield one modulo nine by Taylor and Legendre parity, while z=1 yields A_m via Legendre generating function; an exact binomial scaling modulo nine produces the neighbor-coupled ternary digit rule. A direct six-state transfer has an exact rational generating function with a six-periodic correction. All algebraic divisions are by 3-adic units. The proof is all-depth, and 9,282 exact finite diagnostic tests independently agree with its finite cases; finite tests are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural problem is lifting the universal fixed divisor of the classical Delannoy polynomials from modulus three to its first prime-square modulus nine. The digit-language topology changes from independent allowed digits at the first level to genuine neighboring-digit interactions and an exact six-periodic bounded counting error. A complete simultaneous-evaluation criterion and exact counts support future attempts at higher 3-adic fixed-divisor strata; the result is neither a textbook coefficient reduction nor an arbitrary unmotivated finite slice.
